reviews.text: Less hieratic than Ida, Cold War has a lot to offer to the audience Maybe Pawlikowski would have not won Best Director Award at Cannes if it wasn’t for the sumptuous acting displayed in this cruel, jazz-drenched and Mizoguchi-esque tale of two lovers
reviews.author: Giuseppe Sedia

reviews.text: As the romance gradually evolves, so too does our captive investment in its provocative story and stylish nature.
reviews.author: Calum Cooper

reviews.text: Another stunning work of perfectly placed ellipses and calculated restraint, Pawel Pawlikowski’s Cold War is a film filled with images as iconic and austere as its blunt title.
reviews.author: Greg Carlson

reviews.text: Two fine lead performances drive the central relationship which is filled with intense passion but also missed opportunities at every turn.
reviews.author: Keith Garlington

reviews.text: Cold War has an epic sweep that’s a lyrical gem, almost visually imagistic, and that’s very close to a masterpiece.
reviews.author: M.N. Miller

reviews.text: Cold War marks a huge personal statement by the director, with photography that makes it a scintillating film to watch in HD
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: Episode 16: The Age of Innocence
reviews.author: Taylor Baker

reviews.text: Cold War recalls the visual aesthetic of the Polish Film School, the cinematic movement, inspired in part by Italian neorealism, that flourished in the period of mild liberalization that began in 1956, three years after Stalin's death.
reviews.author: Giles Harvey

reviews.text: An entirely visceral, poetic and unapologetic ode to the essential mystery of love (...) a diamond and a dagger, in one.
reviews.author: Milana Vujkov

reviews.text: Pawel Pawlikowski's magnificently romantic and visually bewitching new film Cold War deals in the secret languages and strange understandings between true lovers
reviews.author: Jason Adams

reviews.text: Its fast pace, coupled with its use of history as an intermittent backdrop to love, is strangely, hauntingly unique.
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: The free expression of love and music is curtailed by a repressive regime [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Gisela Savdie

reviews.text: There's a certain subtleness in film only reached by few. It's that softness mixed with bitter and tension that allows some movies, where the esthetic reigns and the story flows, to become a bona fide exquisiteness. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Victor Pineyro

reviews.text: The bulk of Cold War, Polish director Pawel Pawlikowski's 2018 Academy Award-nominated film, exists in the quiet peripheries.
reviews.author: David Harris

reviews.text: Pawlikowski may have decent artistic instincts, but those prove entirely inadequate in face of the complex questions bound up with the postwar conditions.
reviews.author: Joanne Laurier

reviews.text: Despite an economical running time, Cold War works through a breathtaking range of emotions lived in the moment, and fateful decisions which must be lived with forevermore.
reviews.author: Leigh Paatsch

reviews.text: The result is a film that we respect, even admire, for its technical prowess more than we hold in our hearts. That is unless you hail from Poland, in which case you might get historically emotional.
reviews.author: Jason Fraley

reviews.text: It's an odd concoction at points, breathless but entirely at home within its own lungs.
reviews.author: Matt Cipolla

reviews.text: The ending is beautiful, but I feel like the rest of the film didn't quite earn it.
reviews.author: Dustin Chang

reviews.text: [T]he script ... hints and signifies rather than expressing or emoting. We love the leads not because we know them, but because they're gorgeous.
reviews.author: CJ Sheu

reviews.text: Pawlikowski chisels a poetic, heartbreaking, melancholic romance about a man and a woman who love each other too much, but who are victims of circumstances that symbolize the breakup of a country plagued by political ideologies. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Yasser Medina

reviews.text: Borys Szyc offers an Oscar-worthy turn as an ideology-driven devil.
reviews.author: David Lamble

reviews.text: With a running time of 83 minutes, Cold War is the epitome of economic storytelling at its greatest. In that space of time Pawlikowski manages to tell a passionate epic of grandiose scale.
reviews.author: Charlotte Harrison

reviews.text: Resembling Jennifer Lawrence in her early career, Kulig is certainly a talent to watch out for.
reviews.author: Mina Takla

reviews.text: Its love story is both epic and intimate, personal and political, and one that will haunt you a very long time.
reviews.author: Jeff York

reviews.text: Kulig dazzles as the poised, fearless, unpredictable Zula. Like a little dynamite she's ready to light up any scene with the sheer force of her joy, rage or pain.
reviews.author: Zhuo-Ning Su

reviews.text: The conclusion of Cold War left me anything but cold - I found it to be the sweetest, most romantic ending to a love story ever.
reviews.author: Jaime Davis

reviews.text: Incredibly sexy. It's nice to see a movie that's actually about passion.
reviews.author: Amy Nicholson

reviews.text: Zula and Wiktor age as the years pass, not only in body and attire, but in their very souls, becoming weighed down by political chess games they've been forced to become a part of.
reviews.author: Siddhant Adlakha

reviews.text: There's value in a film like Cold War. However, it's a film I respect more than I actually enjoyed.
reviews.author: Karl Delossantos

reviews.text: Communist Poland in the 1950s is a frigid land of slippery political sands in director Pawel Pawlikowski's graceful, gorgeously retro, black-and-white dedication to his parents.
reviews.author: Andiee Paviour

reviews.text: 'Cold War' is a masterpiece, one of the most wonderful film experiences of the year. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juan Luis Caviaro

reviews.text: The film ... brims with energy, intrigue and eros, and also an abiding love for the films of the second half of the 20th century.
reviews.author: Joe Nolan

reviews.text: My #1 movie of 2018.
reviews.author: Jeff Mitchell

reviews.text: There's a reason it's landed on many year-end Best Of lists and remains a front runner in the Foreign Language Oscar race, and it's because Pawlikowski has crafted a work of art.
reviews.author: Lisa Trifone

reviews.text: Pawlikowski's Cold War is dedicated to his parents, on whose love affair it is loosely based. It is an appropriately beautiful and sympathetic tribute.
reviews.author: John Bleasdale

reviews.text: Cold War is a necessary breath of fresh air. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: William Venegas

reviews.text: Cold War is the arthouse sibling of A Star is Born with its heartbreaking portrait of two lovers on the music scene striving for the future while weighted down by the past.
reviews.author: Pat Mullen

reviews.text: Pawlikowski somehow manages to whip through this decade-and-a-half-long tale in a mere 88 minutes, this all killer, no filler love story at turns reaching right into your heart for squeezes both gentle and much more crushing.
reviews.author: Steve Newall

reviews.text: Compared to other foreign films from around the globe, Cold War is alienating and uninviting despite speaking in the universal language of love.
reviews.author: Dustin Chase

reviews.text: COLD WAR is a remarkable, haunting film about a fiery but doomed romance against the backdrop of history, a film greatly fired up by the two excellent romantic leads and its jazz score.
reviews.author: Cate Marquis

reviews.text: Director Pawel Pawlikowski based this on again, off again love story on his own parents' volatile relationship...This is a beautifully done film that fully develops these two individuals who cannot live with nor without each other.
reviews.author: Linda and Al Lerner

reviews.text: As the old saying goes, "all's fair in love and war," but the existential angst accompanying conflict between nations is more than two people could ever overcome.
reviews.author: Michael J. Casey

reviews.text: Beautiful cinematography, captivating performances, and a doomed love story-what's not to like?
reviews.author: Anna Menta

reviews.text: With changing geography and passage of time, the soundtrack shifts from Polish folk to French jazz to rock 'n' roll. This is one of the highlights of Pawlikowski's homage.
reviews.author: Udita Jhunjhunwala

reviews.text: Their love was meant to be one for the ages, but sometimes shit happens.
reviews.author: Willow Maclay

reviews.text: A couple that can not be separated, but can not be together either. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ernesto Diezmartinez

reviews.text: The dialogue is fascinating and the luscious black-and-white camera work complements it perfectly. And the framing! Oh, the framing!
reviews.author: Jorge Ignacio Castillo

reviews.text: It may be lean narratively, but Cold War packed an emotional punch. A beautiful film that speaks about the complexity of human emotion.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: Cold War contemplates how personal lives are swept up in the tsunami of greater political forces. The result feels even more heartfelt, and for good reason.
reviews.author: Stephen Garrett

reviews.text: There have been a lot of films about singers this year. This one, a Red Star Is Born, counters them by rejecting notions of success from our side of the Iron Curtain.
reviews.author: A.S. Hamrah

reviews.text: This compact romance allows you to marvel at its ravishing visuals while still immersing you in its recreation of Europe in the '50s and '60s.
reviews.author: Rubén Rosario

reviews.text: One of the greatest love stories captured on film. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Iván Belmont

reviews.text: The film distinguishes itself for having an elegant and sumptuous audiovisual experience that sometimes evokes the golden age of Hollywood. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Juanma Fernández París

reviews.text: Patronizes European modernity and turns it into soft-core kitsch.
reviews.author: Armond White

reviews.text: So much passion and fire, and yet so much coldness. Joanna Kulig is a revelation. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Fico Cangiano

reviews.text: Between a sobering score and haunting settings, Pawlikowski has created the perfect backdrop for a maudlin postmortem contemplating the fate of a couple of star-crossed lovers.
reviews.author: Kam Williams

reviews.text: This is a rare film in which everything gels so perfectly, the whole would collapse if one element were missing.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: Pawlikowski renders all this in the same kind of gorgeous black and white that he used in his 2013 film "Ida."
reviews.author: Dan Webster

reviews.text: A mesmerizing performance from Joanna Kulig and beautiful cinematography by Lukasz Zal could not overcome the repugnant nature of a love story centered on a young girl, abused by her father, then controlled and sexualized by her teacher.
reviews.author: Julia Swift

reviews.text: Rarely has a heartfelt film seemed so chilly.
reviews.author: Eleanor Ringel Cater

reviews.text: The film is gorgeous, and [director Pawel] Pawlikowski creates a bleak atmosphere that injects itself into each pristine frame.
reviews.author: Kiko Martinez

reviews.text: There's much to admire about Cold War , a Best Foreign Film nominee for this year's Academy Award.
reviews.author: Wendy Shreve

reviews.text: If all of Hollywood is a form of melodrama, here is its opposite - understated drama that pulls between poignancy and, via its music, a more full-blooded life spirit.
reviews.author: Lynden Barber

reviews.text: Cold War is an immaculately crafted film shot in exquisite black and white and marvelously acted - especially by its incandescent lead actress Joanna Kulig, whose mercurial performance recalls Jeanne Moreau.
reviews.author: John Powers

reviews.text: [Director Pawel] Pawlikowski movies history along with great economy and visual panache.
reviews.author: M. Faust

reviews.text: At a crisp 88 minutes, it's the tightest historical and romantic epic one is likely to see for a long time.
reviews.author: Loren King

reviews.text: Sometimes love is a battlefield. Cold War may leave you feeling like collateral damage.
reviews.author: Rick Kisonak

reviews.text: "Cold War" captivates and transcends barriers of language and culture. It's a gorgeous tale as rocky as it is romantic.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: The brisk pace and short run-time of Cold War add to the fleeting nature of the love story at its center, and each scene feels necessary.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: What makes the film really tick is the two leads - with Kot and Kulig's on screen chemistry feeling almost effortless. The two actors really make you care about the characters and their plights -- furthering the intimate feel of the material.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: Amazingly, Pawlikowski gets there and back in less than 90 minutes by letting us fill in huge time gaps that might take us to even more intriguing places if we legitimately think about it. This seriously is some good, spare stuff.
reviews.author: John Urbancich

reviews.text: Like the great old movie romances, "Cold War" packs a full range of emotions into its narrow frame.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: Since the subtitles are few, fragmented and far-between, for non-linguists, it's frigid and forlorn, evoking a bleak melancholy.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: It may be a "Cold War," but the actors' chemistry burns through the screen.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: A cold, passionless, underwritten tale of a relationship wrecked by circumstance.
reviews.author: Cameron Meier

reviews.text: The best foreign language film of the year, Cold War is a gorgeously sad romance that will leave your heart quaking.
reviews.author: Christopher Lloyd

reviews.text: It's a lot of thematic ground to cover, but it's all conveyed effortlessly in this poignant, poetic film that is never heavy or didactic despite its weighty subjects.
reviews.author: Laura DeMarco

reviews.text: Throughout, though, the tone remains melancholy - and not simply because the film was shot in black and white. An unhappy pall hangs over the movie, keeping the lovers from basking in true happiness.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: Brief nudity, language in romantic, mature Polish drama.
reviews.author: Michael Ordoña

reviews.text: An astute, aggressive inquisition of art as a bureaucratic cudgel gives way to boringly doomed romance -doled out in webisode-sized chunks. Cold War is a gorgeous film to gaze upon, but it's ultimately eye-catching jetsam floating downstream.
reviews.author: Nick Rogers

reviews.text: What was a document of love enduring against all odds becomes one of love's corruptibility. [Pawlikowski has] delivered an exposé on love's power to blind us to everything.
reviews.author: Jared Mobarak

reviews.text: Ms. Kulig's smoldering performance is worth the price of admission in itself. She's clearly channeling Lauren Bacall's laconic-sardonic delivery throughout.
reviews.author: Barry Paris

reviews.text: An artisan masterpiece that reconciles the brevity of haiku with the immensity of a Russian novel. Cold War hits with the strength of an instant classic. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sergio Huidobro

reviews.text: Its Polish folk dancers are a joy to watch.
reviews.author: Harvey S. Karten

reviews.text: This unconventional love story captivates audiences with its nearly square frame and conflicted romance that is amazingly contained to less than 90 minutes without missing a beat or feeling rushed.
reviews.author: Sarah Gopaul

reviews.text: A brilliantly melancholy portrayal of two people who can't resist one another but are doomed to destroy their chance of enduring happiness, as well as the oppressive system they're trapped in.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Pawlowski's masterful and psychologically rich film has its fun moments, but they too, are under a dark cloud. It reflects on the cruelty of European prejudices and nationalism during that period in one of the saddest films in recent memory.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: The movie deftly weaves together the personal and the political.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: Heart-thumping: the passion on display is of all sorts, a steady flame against the cold.
reviews.author: Matthew Lickona

reviews.text: What struck home the most forcefully for me in "Cold War" is its depiction, insidious and unrelenting, of how artists under communism suffered for their art. At its best, the film is like a bulletin from a benighted world.
reviews.author: Peter Rainer

reviews.text: It's gorgeous to look at and, honestly, quite compelling from beginning to end. I just wish I felt more of the love.
reviews.author: Max Weiss

reviews.text: Cold War is filled with remarkably staged scenes that linger in the viewer's consciousness for days.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Edalatpour

reviews.text: In this impossible situation, a powerful but stammering, 15-year love affair gives the movie its emotional weight.
reviews.author: Robert Denerstein

reviews.text: [Cold War] was one of the best films of last year and it is easy to fall in love with.
reviews.author: Beth Accomando

reviews.text: Cold War is meticulously directed, each black-and-white shot composed like a great photograph.
reviews.author: Hannah Brown

reviews.text: Like the time period it covers, this love story is filled with passionate rhetoric and uncertain intentions.
reviews.author: Marjorie Baumgarten

reviews.text: The most ravishing tone poem since Wong Kar-wai's In the Mood for Love.
reviews.author: Ken Eisner

reviews.text: Pawlikowski remains a director to watch and Cold War is a film to watch again and again.
reviews.author: Peter Howell

reviews.text: A sweet romance this isn't, but Pawlikowski (Ida) balances the flatfooted realities of maddeningly thwarted love with swoony moments: smoky jazz clubs and songbird reveries.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: Pawel Pawlikowski's timeless love story seduces the viewer with the perfect blend of romance, tragedy, and music. Joanna Kulig and Tomasz Kot are fantastic.
reviews.author: Joe Friar

reviews.text: This is about as far from Hollywood as one can get and still be in love in every frame.
reviews.author: Tom Meek

reviews.text: The luminous black-and-white musical melodrama is the kind Hollywood used to make, about an attractive couple who sing and fight and love together. Through this lens, it's a kind of romantic protest against a political nightmare.
reviews.author: Liam Lacey

reviews.text: Polish director Pawel Pawlikowski's Cold War is a stunning piece of episodic storytelling that's positively breathtaking in its invigorating emotional magnitude.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: A filmmaking marvel that yields the perfect blend of artistry and passion.
reviews.author: Al Alexander

reviews.text: What the film is doing is recognizing their indelible life force and originality; it's a cri de coeur hurled toward an increasingly hidebound and emotionally stunted era of Western civilization.
reviews.author: Andrea Gronvall

reviews.text: Much like Ida, the film is shot in gorgeous black & white by cinematographer Lukasz Zal, giving the feel you're watching some piece of history passed on across generations.
reviews.author: Travis Hopson

reviews.text: Poland has seen more than its share of war, and of the art and cinema of exile. Pawel Pawlikowski's latest feature, Cold War, is a spirited albeit flawed entry in this category.
reviews.author: Ela Bittencourt

reviews.text: Filled with music from many genres, from folk to jazz to rock and roll, Pawel Pawlikowski's Cold War is a sumptuous, sad, and often thrilling story of love set mostly in post-war Poland.
reviews.author: Peg Aloi

reviews.text: When together, they are madly in love, fight a lot, and make beautiful jazz. The film has a perfect ending.
reviews.author: Charles Mudede

reviews.text: Slightly cold to the touch...Cold War is a visually striking black-and-white musical drama, beautifully shot by cinematographer Łukasz Żal.
reviews.author: Michael Ward

reviews.text: Complex, lushly black-and-white love story may be Oscar foreign language front runner.
reviews.author: James Verniere

reviews.text: A marvel of concision. The story skips like a stone across time, to devastating effect.
reviews.author: Sean Burns

reviews.text: It's as verbally spare as it is visually spellbinding.
reviews.author: Michael Phillips

reviews.text: If Kulig, who resembles Jessica Chastain, were American, Hollywood would be offering her everything.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: Along with the off-center black-and-white cinematography, Pawlikoski's most effective tool here is the way music provides the pulse of the story.
reviews.author: Robert Horton

reviews.text: Cold War is a concise and dry and amusingly romantic tale that takes its storytelling to a daringly elliptical fashion and it thankfully pays off, as it convincingly shows how fleeting memories of love can be and yet can stand the test of time.
reviews.author: Harris Dang

reviews.text: Cold War is also about art itself, and the conditions necessary for its creation. Art is always a balance of freedom and constraint, and these two artists find their balance differently...
reviews.author: Claire Messud

reviews.text: This picture feels like a film out of time, shot in glorious black-and-white with a steady camera and careful compositions.
reviews.author: Sherilyn Connelly

reviews.text: "Cold War" suffices as a simple filmic jewel of a story, about a couple swimming hard against the currents of history and governments until they only have each other to cling to.
reviews.author: Ty Burr

reviews.text: Cold War has the heart of an epic, a smart one, burrowing into its settings, and describing the bitter flavor of two different brands of moral crumble.
reviews.author: Richard von Busack

reviews.text: [Director Pawel] Pawlikowski has the knack of making personal (and political) heartbreak seem, initially, like a joyous European fling.
reviews.author: Kelly Vance

reviews.text: "Cold War" is a near-perfect film, an artfully crafted, flawlessly acted meditation on love, memory and invented history that's both deeply personal and politically attuned.
reviews.author: Ann Hornaday

reviews.text: Cinematographer Lukasz Zal finds a chilly, etched beauty in every frame; you're struck by how snow seems to stroke and soften a harsh landscape, and by the poignancy of wind ruffling the grass in a quiet field.
reviews.author: Moira MacDonald

reviews.text: Through "Cold War," Pawlikowski shows us the beauty in an ugly time, and then he makes us wait and wonder if the characters will ever see it, too.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: "Cold War" devastates all the same, and its meditations on what might have been and what could never be haunt long after the gutting final frame.
reviews.author: Barbara VanDenburgh

reviews.text: The love story between a woman and an older man is one that you've seen many times onscreen before, but there's something about the stark black and white visuals and the sparse narrative that deliver a bittersweet emotional punch.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: A gorgeous depiction of reckless, headlong, decades-long love... The gorgeous, sweeping story isn't so much elliptical as a succession of sensations, of emotional fragrance told in songs... and shimmering black-and-white images.
reviews.author: Ray Pride

reviews.text: Cold War is a beautiful showcasing of unbreakable and incomparably dedicated romance capable of strengthening the bond between any couple that watches it
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Pawlikowski's latest is particularly memorable for its sweeping scope, some heady sensuality and the performances of the broodingly handsome Kot and Kulig, who could use this as a calling-card to hit Hollywood, if she fancies stooping that low.
reviews.author: David 'Mad Dog' Bradley

reviews.text: Cold War, like Ida before it, harkens back to midcentury world cinema, resuscitating its distinctly philosophical outlook while remaining current today and likely for decades to come.
reviews.author: Alex Leininger

reviews.text: Kulig commands the camera, but "Cold War" kept me at an emotional distance.
reviews.author: Laura Clifford

reviews.text: It's an understated achievement of great elegance and awareness of the intractable illogic of people. As cinema, it's near perfect, but there's many another schlockier romance that actually makes us care about its lovers.
reviews.author: Rob Gonsalves

reviews.text: Political freedom, long dreamed of, brings little release.
reviews.author: Anthony Lane

reviews.text: Married with the Academy ratio, the color scheme makes the film feel classic, but Pawlikowski's desire to plumb his past makes it timeless.
reviews.author: Andy Crump

reviews.text: By downplaying the romance and not accompanying each embrace with a swelling saxophone, Pawlikowski paradoxically makes Cold War even more romantic.
reviews.author: Jordan Riefe

reviews.text: It is a lean and perfect gem.
reviews.author: Graeme Tuckett

reviews.text: A love story that feels strangled by history, a character study and historical tone poem that triumphs on both of those levels.
reviews.author: Tim Brayton

reviews.text: Wrapped in deepest melancholy, Cold War has no idle or frivolous scenes since everything fits and flows under Pawlikowski's masterful direction.
reviews.author: Filipe Freitas

reviews.text: Like a song, a relationship can change depending on the context. Pawlikowski approaches this premise and created one of the most personal and masterful films of the year.
reviews.author: Alan French

reviews.text: It's an anthology of disillusions in which love is the only transcendent force.
reviews.author: John McDonald

reviews.text: An old-fashioned melodrama -- a good one at that.
reviews.author: Stuart Klawans

reviews.text: Much like the folk songs heard throughout the film, Polish director Pawel Pawlikowski's romantic tragedy takes a story of heartbreak and horror and transforms it into something beautiful and timeless.
reviews.author: Daniel Barnes

reviews.text: You lap up the images of these beautiful actors, whose textures and feelings are enhanced by the film's overall beauty. And then you wonder if there isn't something missing.
reviews.author: K. Austin Collins

reviews.text: Cold War is seductive and yet there is darkness at its heart, one that elevates the Polish film into a thoughtful piece about the complexities of love in a time of political oppression.
reviews.author: Wenlei Ma

reviews.text: The small moments linger the most throughout Cold War, and it's in those delicate notes that Pawlikowski's film gains its true resonance.
reviews.author: Dominick Suzanne-Mayer

reviews.text: This bittersweet romance is richly textured and quietly powerful.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Thunderously dull romantic drama from Paweł Pawlikowski, who won a best foreign film Oscar for 2015's Ida...it's a slog, as well as featuring characters who are hard enough to relate to without Pawlikowski's sterile direction.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: A film about a doomed romance, Cold War is a haunting portrait of love during wartime, a love that's maybe not meant to be but utterly, cosmically, inescapable.
reviews.author: Joshua Brunsting

reviews.text: Although it leaves you wanting more, Cold War is a film that is both illuminating and haunting at the same time.
reviews.author: Rex Reed

reviews.text: Cold War is an unconventional yet deeply moving love story that feels like a modern classic.
reviews.author: Marisa Carpico

reviews.text: Cold War is constructed with brief but always telling scenes. It wastes no time, and indeed the running time is shorter than usual. But every moment packs a punch, and every musical cue serves an important purpose.
reviews.author: David Stratton

reviews.text: Detente has never been so deadly, nor so perverse.
reviews.author: Christopher Llewellyn Reed

reviews.text: Though 'Cold War' falls far short of its predecessor, it still has enough striking moments to recommend it.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: It's the love stories like the one inCold War (Zimna wojna) that have the ability to transcend time by offering us the most meaningful impact.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: Wiktor says that Zula is "the woman of my life." He's not lying, and that's what makes this anti-romance ... so mundanely tragic...
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: This is a masterful, romantic movie filled with stunning imagery, gorgeous use of folk music and jazz and you won't find a false moment in the entire running time. Probably a classic-to-be, certainly first-class moviemaking.
reviews.author: Stephen Rebello

reviews.text: Passionate, tempestuous, haunting and assured, this latest from writer-director Pawel Pawlikowski explores, as did his Oscar-winning "Ida," Poland's recent past, resulting in a potent emotional story with political overtones that plays impeccably today.
reviews.author: Kenneth Turan

reviews.text: Cold War is an ode to joylessness that feels historically credible but narratively arbitrary.
reviews.author: Mark Jenkins

reviews.text: The film is on a par with that other black-and-white foreign Oscar contender Roma, only more exciting.
reviews.author: Tim Appelo

reviews.text: It's Pawlikowski second-straight masterwork, only one with a critical if seldom-seen error. His movie is too short.
reviews.author: Jake Coyle

reviews.text: Its greatest strengths, though, are its two knockout leads, who give the story its heat, its flesh and its heartbreak.
reviews.author: Manohla Dargis

reviews.text: Pawlikowski maintains a high level of energy with frequent music performances, subtle comedy, and a pitch-perfect bittersweet ending.
reviews.author: Alan Zilberman

reviews.text: Pawel Pawlikowski's savagely sexy spellbinder burns with a fever that won't quit. Joanna Kulig is a shining new star who rips across the screen like a comet. Forget the frosty title, there's enough sizzling carnality here to the singe the screen.
reviews.author: Peter Travers

reviews.text: ... Cold War is not a typical love story in which its leads are wonderful people triumphing against all odds to prove their love is real. Rather ... Cold War feels more real in its depiction of a hard love set in hard times.
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: Watching the film is a hypnotic experience. Part of that is surely due to the star power of Joanna Kulig, who Pawlikowski gives a luscious showcase to.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: Cold War resembles a waking dream. And a ravishingly romantic one at that.
reviews.author: Chris Nashawaty

reviews.text: It's fair to argue that there's more truth in Cold War than in many love stories - that, although a romantic attachment isn't the best basis for a long-term relationship, its power cannot be denied or set aside.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: An aching film on such exquisite pains of impossible love, Paweł Pawlikowski's Cold War concurrently swells your heart and breaks it.
reviews.author: Tomris Laffly

reviews.text: Love is a losing game. But not always. Or maybe always. Watch this audiovisual game of love. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Guillem Martinez Oya

reviews.text: It's rare to see a love story built on two such complex individuals, each with their own desires and flaws... They move in tandem, a choreographed dance that brings them together, and pulls them apart, only to jerk back, like magnets.
reviews.author: Anne Cohen

reviews.text: It's a lot of movie, and represents tremendous value if your time is tight. The love story ... is such a good one ... that it verges on the preposterous. It's not. It's based on Pawlikowski's own parents, and that tips it over into the miraculous.
reviews.author: CJ Johnson

reviews.text: This new Pawlikowski films lacks heat... however, it gives us one of the best romances in recent years. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: Cold War resonates thanks to Joanna Kulig's brilliant performance.
reviews.author: Courtney Small

reviews.text: If you want an uplifting entertainment, go and see Mary Poppins this Christmas. But if you want cinema that challenges and digs into your soul, catch a Cold War.
reviews.author: Andrew L. Urban

reviews.text: As bleak as it is beautiful, Pawel Pawlikowski's melancholy film is an ode to love.
reviews.author: Louise Keller

reviews.text: Pawel Pawlikowski delivers a beautifully-searing masterpiece.
reviews.author: Ben Rolph

reviews.text: Pawel Pawlikowski is in love with his characters, his story, and the world he's built in Cold War, and it shows in every frame.
reviews.author: Mike Reyes

reviews.text: Passionate and episodic love story between mismatched lovers who are meant for each other but that may not be enough.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: What most engrossed me in Cold War was the framing. The square frame envelops you and focuses your eye more so than even widescreen or IMAX movies often do.
reviews.author: Fred Topel

reviews.text: In a visually stunning, formally immaculate and darkly romantic film, Pawel Pawlikowski sets a story of star-crossed lovers against the turmoil of post-war Europe.
reviews.author: Erica Abeel

reviews.text: For Wiktor and Zula, their devotion to each other is the one thing in their world not built on sand.
reviews.author: David Bax

reviews.text: Pawlikowski continues to be a master of frame composition. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: It's got more energy and freedom than the more classically told Ida, and this can be seen in the camera movements, although occasionally it feels like the movie meanders as much as the characters do.
reviews.author: Kaleem Aftab

reviews.text: Pawlikowski is compelling his two lovers on a sadistic and slightly contrived trajectory to end-gain the moral of the story which is that corrosive politics destroy lives.
reviews.author: PJ Nabarro

reviews.text: In Cold War, every frame contains a moving beauty and intensity. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: Pawel Pawlikowski puts on stage what is impossible to represent: the space for love in a world divided in two, in this masterful work, powerful and reflective, about passions denied by the historical context. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Emiliano Basile

reviews.text: It's sort of Richard Linklater's Before trilogy meets Casablanca, but condensed into an all-too-short 85-minute runtime.
reviews.author: Matthew Dougherty

reviews.text: The detail is absolutely stunning, there's a searing authenticity to the time period that is undeniably absorbing...However, the almost too tightening restraint forces us to quickly witness its events rather than be moved by them.
reviews.author: Jordan Ruimy

reviews.text: Pawlikowski knows that we know this story from other movies (A Star is Born, New York New York), so he strips away the externals, and trains his spotlight on the bare basics.
reviews.author: Baradwaj Rangan

reviews.text: The era is set impeccably and the two lead performances are attractive to watch. Eighty-eight minutes roll by and the dirge-like pace zaps the fun and life out of the tale.
reviews.author: Dwight Brown

reviews.text: Never genuinely getting to the root of their love, what the viewer is left with is a yearning for more but wrapped in a riveting performance from Joanna Kulig.
reviews.author: Clayton Davis

reviews.text: Cold War is an imperfect work, evoking a sublime beauty despite its clichés, and cliched despite its sublime beauty.
reviews.author: Lauren Humphries-Brooks

reviews.text: It's as though the scriptwriters already knew the ending ... The result: elliptical and underwritten storytelling.
reviews.author: Kent Turner

reviews.text: From the musical start, until in one of the most beautiful, romantic and tragic outcomes that I have seen in the cinema, this film is unpredictable, powerful, lyrical, complex and truthful. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Boyero

reviews.text: The unique find is that relationship between background and form that evokes the commitment of this couple. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Carlos Marañón

reviews.text: Pawlikowski gives us only the bare essentials, making sure they look (and sound) as stunning as possible.
reviews.author: Tomas Trussow

reviews.text: Pawel Pawlikowski paints a crude and rough mural in which it is seen, between the winter fog of its separated chapters a love story in which, consequently, we can not intervene ... And it has a reason. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Erick Estrada

reviews.text: Luminously shot in black and white, with every frame artfully composed, Pawel Pawlikowski's powerful "Cold War"....casts a spell over audiences.
reviews.author: Gary M. Kramer

reviews.text: For all the effort on display, it's hard to shake the feeling that this isn't a little too easy for Pawlikowski who... ultimately delivers a desaturated version of The English Patient's more hard-won story of the violence.
reviews.author: Angelo Muredda

reviews.text: This is a movie in which the political is personal: what separates Wiktor and Zula is less the Iron Curtain than an intractable cold war of the heart.
reviews.author: Tony Rayns

reviews.text: A passionate love story (yes, there's a recurrent theme here) that plays out, with musical accompaniment and political resonance, across three decades in postwar Europe.
reviews.author: Joe Morgenstern

reviews.text: Cold War is a self-indulgent and mostly lifeless endeavor that could only exist within the context of a film festival.
reviews.author: David Nusair

reviews.text: While it's true that the problems of two little people don't amount to more than a hill of beans in Stalin's USSR, they're real enough to the people experiencing them. We feel for them, even if the world can't.
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: Form and content seem oddly divorced, but music -- the Polish folk tunes, communist-propaganda anthems and Parisian torch songs -- sets the mood and saves the day.
reviews.author: Kate Taylor

reviews.text: For all his allusions to the contrary, [director Pawe] Pawlikowski may be contemporary cinema's foremost metteur en scène.
reviews.author: Jordan Cronk

reviews.text: Cold War deserves to be a hit - one of the year's best singles, perhaps, if not an album.
reviews.author: Tom Shone

reviews.text: If the sudden unresolved ending disappoints it's only because we'd like the whole thing to go on much longer.
reviews.author: Matthew Bond

reviews.text: While one can't reproach Pawlikowski for lacking authenticity, their constant bickering and falling out makes one question whether they should be together at all, with nothing substantial... underpinning their love, just raw erotic energy.
reviews.author: Maximilian Von Thun

reviews.text: Unexpectedly put me in mind of Casablanca or La La Land as reimagined by Andrzej Wajda or Agnieszka Holland - a reminder of the fundamental things that apply, as time goes by.
reviews.author: Mark Kermode

reviews.text: Without any hyperbole, it is one of the films of the year, and possibly of the last decade.
reviews.author: Hilary A White

reviews.text: This lush throwback to European cinema of the 1950s and 60 looks gorgeous and sounds wonderful, but it never quite gels as the passionate romance it wants to be.
reviews.author: MaryAnn Johanson

reviews.text: The exquisitely-told tale of a decades-long love affair that defies boundaries of class and age, as well as post-war tensions between East and West.
reviews.author: Brian Viner

reviews.text: All the ingredients are there, but it doesn't quite come together.
reviews.author: David Jenkins

reviews.text: This is a remarkable achievement - sumptuous, ambitious, intelligent and with a knockout soundtrack.
reviews.author: Edward Lawrenson

reviews.text: Cold War is 88 minutes of thermal underwear looking for a full outfit of winter ideas.
reviews.author: Nigel Andrews

reviews.text: The whole nature of Cold War is one of abbreviation: snappy editing, temporal jumps, deliberately unresolved emotions... This is a film of glancing, heart-crushing pleasures.
reviews.author: Ryan Gilbey

reviews.text: When the film came to an end, all I wanted was to watch it all over again; Cold War is the first really great film of 2018.
reviews.author: Saskia Baron

reviews.text: At an intense 88 minutes, it's truly all killer, no filler.
reviews.author: Larushka Ivan-Zadeh

reviews.text: Pawlikowski is in complete control of the form, but this is no austere piece of work - he even finds time for a few good jokes. Accessible, humane and compassionate: what a treat this is.
reviews.author: Andrew Lowry

reviews.text: One of the most colourful things you'll ever see in black and white.
reviews.author: Philip De Semlyen

reviews.text: Pawlikowski manages another masterful presentation of doomed humans struggling to outrun a past which will not let them go in a film as beautifully packaged as it is performed.
reviews.author: Nicholas Bell

reviews.text: [Pawlikowski] has a singular voice all his own, unfurling this story with a lyrical grace that mixes passion, pain and humour with profound political awareness.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Full of aching, ecstasy and anger, this is a remarkable and beautiful film about a love that is possible only when it borders on the impossible.
reviews.author: Karl Quinn

reviews.text: It's far from a misfire, but it is a grand epic deserving of a far grander canvas than this.
reviews.author: Alistair Ryder

reviews.text: [Director Pawel] Pawlikowski is taciturn, romantic and hopeless in equal parts, he lets himself be carried away by moments of incredible happiness that will be destroyed by the cruel reality of an irrevocable destiny. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Alberto Sáez Villarino

reviews.text: This is a film that understands the intensity and complexity of a true connection as it reverberates through the years.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: An utterly devastating exploration of love, loyalty, politics and survival.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: A tableaux of gorgeous idylls alternate with passages of music and dance
reviews.author: Lawrence Garcia

reviews.text: The ominous figure of socialism chases this love story throughout and is composed with sharp plastic rigor as well as a sensibility akin to the feminine characters of Ingmar Bergman. [Full Review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge (JJ) Negrete

reviews.text: Cold War rivals most films I can think of in how much longing it packs into every scene... It's a work of unspeakable beauty.
reviews.author: Alissa Wilkinson

reviews.text: This is an achingly personal story - the romantic leads are named after Pawlikowski's own parents, to whom the film is dedicated - and also a sadly resigned one.
reviews.author: Justin Chang

reviews.text: Cold War will only increase Pawlikowski's reputation as one of the next great auteurs, but, more importantly, it will have everyone who sees it asking, "What's that girl's name?" Ladies and gentlemen, her name is Joanna Kulig has she has arrived.
reviews.author: Gregory Ellwood

reviews.text: The more we see this relationship, the more its mystery grows. That is the profound, beguiling truth with which Cold War ultimately leaves us.
reviews.author: Bilge Ebiri

reviews.text: As a romance, Cold War wobbles, but the allegory that the pairing represent is sharply defined and suitably harrowing.
reviews.author: Gus Edgar

reviews.text: It deftly walks the line between appropriately somber and great, sophisticated fun.
reviews.author: Stephanie Zacharek

reviews.text: Pawlikowski gives us a musical romance that works through all the minor keys that matter. Will look and sound well everywhere.
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: A haunted postwar epic in miniature, like a novel written with the careful, precise economy of a short story.
reviews.author: A.A. Dowd

reviews.text: The final result is an admirable exercise of narrative economy but also a beautiful love story. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Àngel Quintana

reviews.text: It's a brave thing, to tell a story by omission, but Pawlikowski almost pulls it off.
reviews.author: David Ehrlich

reviews.text: Demonstrates a significant leap in storytelling prowess together with an unerring ability to convey the most revealing character traits with the tiniest of details.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: Reflecting the two leads, the film retains a quiet humour throughout.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: In 84 densely packed minutes, the dialogue is often bracingly spare and scenes of sensual pleasure are invariably interrupted, as if cut off by the long arm of cold war communism.
reviews.author: Raphael Abraham

reviews.text: Pawlikowski's finest work to date, it's a dexterous examination of two juxtaposed ideologies wrapped in a mesmerising story of wounded love.
reviews.author: Joseph Walsh

reviews.text: Shot in ravishing black and white, it offers a stunning marriage of haunting imagery and heartfelt emotion.
reviews.author: Allan Hunter

reviews.text: The film is most exhilarating as a breathless vessel for mood, one that just so happens to conduct itself within reconstructed period settings that are as obsessively detailed as the reverently curated soundtrack.
reviews.author: Sam C. Mac

reviews.text: It's visually stunning, passionate, wistful, and thoughtful in equal measure.
reviews.author: Emily Yoshida

reviews.text: At its heart there's a relationship that doesn't wholly move you as it needs to do. The rigour of this film-making is nonetheless ravishing.
reviews.author: David Sexton

reviews.text: There is an exquisite chill to this film.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: This film fizzes with a devotional energy and political relevance.
reviews.author: Nick James

reviews.text: Gives us a vision of a Poland in which everyone is a hardened survivor of conflict, where bridges have been crossed and one more betrayal or bargain for self-advancement is just another in a long line of similar events.
reviews.author: Fionnuala Halligan

reviews.text: A soberly moving study of the disappointment and insecurity that can blossom from supposed renewal: It's a romance in which new beginnings and endings can be hard to tell apart.
reviews.author: Guy Lodge

reviews.text: A thrilling exploration of romantic disappointment with a killer soundtrack.
reviews.author: Leslie Felperin

reviews.text: Somehow, it's both pristine and jazzy - emotionally aloof by design, but still accessible.
reviews.author: Tim Robey

synopsis: Set against the backdrop of the 1950s Cold War in Poland, two people of differing backgrounds and temperaments begin an almost impossible romance.
